Mathieu stared out the window, wishing he was back home. He was scared. Not only because of where he was going, but also because of the method of getting there. He father sat beside him, quiet and stubborn. He had barely spoken to him since this morning. Mathieu's seat shook, making him feel sick. He looked out of the window once more to see a vast expanse of blue. The plane had only been in the air for ten minutes, but he already hated it. The small propeller plane looked to have been outdated 50 years ago. He closed his eyes, trying to get some sleep.

It was raining when they landed. The rain was coming down in long rods, soaking anyone who dared to leave shelter. Mathieu had only been to the mainland once, for his uncle's wedding. He hadn't liked it then and he certainly wasn't liking it now. His father had had enough of his problems at school he was been sent to live with his great-aunt in Port Louis. The taxi arrived after a 20 minute wait and Mathieu got in while his father put his suitcase in the boot.It was only a fifteen minute taxi ride to Mathieu's great aunt's house. It was a small, modest home, similar to his own. It was at that point that the emotion of the situation got to Mathieu. His eyes started to fill with tears. He would miss Vingt Cinq, even his school.

Mathieu's father got his suitcase out of the taxi, and then proceeded to walk towards the front door. 'Papa, please! I don't want to live here! Let me come home with you!'. All Mathieu got from his father was a cold look and he knocked on the door. A plump, friendly looking woman opened the door. 'Hello Mathieu, Davide. Please come in. Mathieu, why don't you go sit in the living room, just on the left, while I talk to your father'. Mathieu did as he was asked and shuffled into the living room. A pretty, blonde woman was sat on the sofa. 'Hello, who are you?' she said in a strange accent. 'Mathieu'. He sat down next to the woman. Mathieu winced as he made contact with the leather. He was still sore from when he had been punished by his father. 'Don't worry about living here, Mrs Darvi is a lovely woman'. The woman finished the rest of her coffee and got up to leave. 'See you later Mrs Darvi, I have to go now' she shouted into the kitchen. A muffled voice called back: 'Ok love, I'll see you next week. Bye Anna'. A few minutes later, Mathieu heard the front door open and then shut again. That was it, he was stuck in a strange place with nobody who he knew. But in his gut he felt things would turn out alright. Anna had said that she was a nice woman and Mathieu trusted her.
